segments.expected: "I know you did." Lyle got up. She had the towel round her neck. "She's been at it since six," she said, without looking at Carrow. "Treen calls, and she lights. "She's very good at it already. She's good at everything she hates."

segments.expected: She had known it would not. She had known it at the table at eleven with the chalk in Perrin's fist, and said it, and Perrin had said wrist, then, and she had said wrist. But a wrist under a pole is not a hand round it, and the head of the Commodore came over the hazel at her and she took it on her left hand and her right wrist and it went down on the right. Pru had the foot. Pru had put her capped fingers round the foot poles, because that was where the foot was. Kiva heard her draw her breath in through her teeth.

segments.expected: After that the Tarn tried three things, and Kiva learned something from each. First they tried to drag the foot, with their Hold and their catcher on the foot poles together, and Anwen's wall came up on the south side between them and the rest of the pen. Anwen did not lean it on anybody. She held it there, low and silver, a door with somebody standing behind it, and the Tarn could drag the foot round in an arc but not away. A planted head and a dragged foot made a litter turn on its own length like a gate on its hinge.

When did you lift? said Ask.

segments.expected: "I didn't," he began, and stopped, because Aske was looking at him over his spectacles with no expression whatever. "At the spur," he said. "Yesterday. The boards. When they carried him up the bank. I took the head of the boards at the lip, for the last two paces. They'd have had to set him down on the stones otherwise." He swallowed. "I knew I shouldn't. I knew it while I was doing it. I'd like it known that I'd do it again."

segments.expected: They were big. Everybody from the Tarn was big, as if the hills grew them on purpose. Their captain was a thin dark girl with a still door, who walked as though the stone under her were a field she knew. The others came behind her: a heavy blade, a Hold with long arms, a catcher with a fresh bandage on one wrist. They stood behind their hurdle and looked down the pen at Seven, and Kiva saw them look at the linen on her right hand, and Pru's ten caps, and Jude's left arm hanging, and Perrin standing outside the pen with his hand pressed to his side.
